trigger_condition: vscodeClaudeCode target configured on win32 (VS Code already installed or freshly installed)
potential_consequence: vscodePath is already the Code.exe file path; join(vscodePath,'bin','code.cmd') builds a nonexistent nested path, so the extension install always fails

trigger_condition: Extension install step execs a path ending in .cmd on win32 with default shell:false
guard_snippet: exec(cli, ['--install-extension', CLAUDE_CODE_EXTENSION], { timeout: EXTENSION_TIMEOUT_MS, shell: process.platform === 'win32' })
potential_consequence: Spawning a .cmd file without shell:true fails on Windows (same gotcha the codebase already documents for npm.cmd/npx.cmd in src/utils/processes.ts), so code.cmd never actually runs

trigger_condition: ensureClientsInstalled checks whether ChatGPT (codex-desktop) is installed on win32
guard_snippet: if (app === 'codex-desktop') return [join(programFiles, 'WindowsApps', '...ChatGPT...')]; // or drop the Store-only short-circuit's reliance on this helper
potential_consequence: windowsApplicationDirs has no case for 'codex-desktop' (returns []), so findInstalledClient always reports it as not installed, making the Store-only error fire even when ChatGPT is already installed

trigger_condition: installClient()/installClientWindows() is called directly (bypassing client-install-step.ts's codex-desktop win32 guard) for an app with no Windows support
guard_snippet: if (!spec.winBundle || windowsApplicationDirs(spec.app).length === 0) throw fail(`${spec.label} cannot be installed on Windows from the CLI.`);
potential_consequence: destDir falls back to homedir() and bundle falls back to the macOS spec.bundle (e.g. 'ChatGPT.app'), silently writing to the wrong place and trying to run a non-Windows package as installer.exe

trigger_condition: winget manifest's picked installer entry has no InstallerSha256, or Installers key is missing/renamed
guard_snippet: if (!picked.InstallerSha256) throw new Error('installer has no published checksum'); if (!Array.isArray(manifest?.Installers)) throw new Error('unexpected winget manifest shape');
potential_consequence: Empty/missing sha256 silently skips checksum verification in downloadToFile (no equivalent to macOS's codesign check exists), or a schema change throws an opaque TypeError instead of a ClientInstallError

trigger_condition: Windows installer executable has no signature/authenticity check analogous to macOS's verifyBundle+teamId gate
guard_snippet: // after download: verify Authenticode signer, or at minimum refuse to run when download.sha256 is absent
potential_consequence: An unverified or tampered Windows installer can be executed silently under the user's account with no vendor-identity check

trigger_condition: GitHub contents API lists a non-version-named entry (file, README, pre-release dir) alongside version directories
potential_consequence: compareVersions(a,b) returns NaN for non-numeric segments, which can corrupt the sort and pick the wrong 'latest' manifest directory

trigger_condition: The matching user-scope, non-MSIX installer entry is actually type msi/zip/wix rather than a directly runnable exe
potential_consequence: A non-executable installer type is saved as installer.exe and handed to run(), which fails with a confusing exec error instead of a clear 'unsupported installer type' message

trigger_condition: Windows installer process exits 0 before (or without) actually placing winBundle at the predicted dest (Squirrel-style installers are explicitly called out as unconfirmed in the surrounding comment)
guard_snippet: if (!existsSync(dest)) throw fail(`${spec.label} installer finished but ${dest} was not found.`);
potential_consequence: installClientWindows reports success and returns a path that doesn't exist yet, so the next step (e.g. VS Code extension install) fails with a misleading error instead of a clear install-verification failure
